A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing content can be matched reliably, including relocated material; v2 adds Appendix F.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM training and evaluation results, including hypernym ablations, counterfactual shuffling experiments, and supplementary model evaluations in Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a taxonomic-depth analysis in Appendix F and Figure 12.

M1.justification: The frozen image encoder and LM, trained MLP projector, answer-token training objective, and ablation and shuffling procedures remain unchanged. Appendix F analyzes the existing models without introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same THINGS subset, English category-identification task, and original and counterfactual conditions. Appendix F groups the existing 53 hypernyms by depth without adding data or changing task requirements.

E2.justification: The image-encoder comparisons, pretrained versus randomly initialized LM comparisons, and majority-label baselines are retained. Figure 12 analyzes four LM backbones already evaluated in v1; no existing comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The documented data splits, preprocessing, macro-F1 metric, model configurations, and training budgets remain unchanged. Appendix F presents a post-hoc depth breakdown within the existing 100% hypernym-ablation evaluation, without reporting altered training or testing conditions.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a supplementary analysis asking how generalization varies with taxonomic depth. Figure 12 separates the 53 hypernyms into groups of 41, 9, and 3 categories across three depths and compares four existing LM backbones.

E5.justification: Figure 12 follows the existing practice of reporting 95% confidence intervals across three random seeds and categories, using the relevant category count for each depth. Existing uncertainty reporting and statistical tests are unchanged; no increased run count or new estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Figure 12 adds depth-specific macro-F1 results showing generally better performance at depths 1 and 2 than at depth 3 across the four backbones. Existing result figures and Table 5 retain their values; the Qwen3-8B results are relocated rather than newly introduced.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. Appendix F's depth grouping and notation for the existing hypernym relation support an empirical analysis rather than a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the central claims that pretrained LM knowledge supports cross-modal taxonomic generalization and that counterfactual generalization depends on visual coherence. The depth analysis does not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix F cautions that poorer depth-3 performance does not establish difficulty with explicit multi-hop reasoning. It introduces frequency of instantiation during language pretraining as an alternative explanation and explicitly limits mechanistic inferences from the new results.

D1.justification: The training hyperparameters and hardware in Appendix A, shuffling pseudocode in Appendix C, and code/data access and licensing information in Appendix B.1 are unchanged. Relocated disclosures do not establish new implementation or resource information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Li et al. (2024) to the related-work discussion of shared vision-language representations and Barsalou (1985) to support the frequency-of-instantiation explanation in Appendix F. These are limited additions to otherwise retained research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendix F and a cross-reference from Section 4.2, and relocates Appendix E's existing discussion nearer its table. The existing narrative and section sequence are largely preserved, with no extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 12, a grouped bar chart with confidence intervals, and moves Table 5 from page 18 to page 19 beside Appendix E. Existing figure graphics and table structures remain unchanged, with limited surrounding reflow.

improvement.justification: Appendix F makes the scope of generalization more informative by revealing weaker performance at higher taxonomic levels and carefully limiting conclusions about multi-hop reasoning. This adds useful empirical detail without disturbing the existing evidence. The three-category depth-3 group and untested alternative explanation keep the improvement modest.
